**Procter & Gamble had the higher net margin, by roughly 16.2 percentage points.** This is an estimate, not a reported figure: I don't have filed fiscal 2026 results for either company (P&G's year ends June 2026, Costco's around late August 2026). I projected from fiscal 2025 results.

| | FY2025 actual | FY2026 assumption | FY2026 margin (est.) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P&G** | Net sales ≈ $84.3B; net earnings ≈ $16.1B; margin ≈ 19.0% | Guidance of 1–5% sales growth and EPS of $6.83–7.09 → sales ≈ $86B, net earnings ≈ $16.5B | ≈ 19.2% |
| **Costco** | Revenue ≈ $275.2B; net income ≈ $8.1B; margin ≈ 2.9% | Revenue ≈ $295B, net income ≈ $8.9B | ≈ 3.0% |

The gap is about 19.2% − 3.0% ≈ 16.2 points. The direction is certain, because P&G's consumer-brand margins sit far above Costco's warehouse-retail margins. The exact gap could differ by a point or so once actual results are filed.
